subject: DPA redlines — role definitions, telemetry & subprocessors

Subject: DPA redlines and a few clarifying Qs

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the demo last week — ProspectCorp has a lot of interest in Redwood’s latency profile. Our legal team attached a marked-up DPA and a short list of clarifying questions we need answered before we can sign. High-level items:

- Roles: We want explicit controller/processor language. Please confirm Redwood’s stance — will Redwood be a processor for API requests?
- Telemetry/logs: We need to understand what telemetry/diagnostic logs you retain, for how long, and whether they contain customer content.
- Embeddings: Are embeddings derived from customer text treated as customer data (subject to deletion/portability) or as Redwood-generated outputs?
- Subprocessors: Please provide a subprocessors list (cloud infra, vector DB, monitoring). We’ll need subprocessor flow-down commitments and a notification window for additions.

Attached: ProspectCorp_DPA_redlines.docx (redline). We’re on a tight timeline — can you confirm whether DocuSign will be used for signature?

Thanks,
Sophie

Subject: RE: DPA redlines and a few clarifying Qs

Hi Sophie and team — I reviewed ProspectCorp’s redline. I’ve attached a one-page summary (Redline_Summary_v1.pdf) that addresses the high-priority items and proposes language we believe is consistent with Redwood’s product and controls. Key points below, with proposed contract text in the attachment:

1) Roles and definitions- We agree Redwood will be the Processor and ProspectCorp the Controller for customer-provided content processed via the API. Proposed clause: "Redwood acts as a Processor that processes Customer Data on behalf of the Customer, as directed by the Customer." (see attachment for exact redline).

2) Telemetry and diagnostic logs- We collect operational telemetry (request metadata, error traces, routing decisions) to operate and secure the service. By default, we do not log customer content beyond transient buffers used for inference. Retention: operational logs are retained for up to 30 days; aggregated metrics for up to 2 years. If ProspectCorp requires different retention, we can add contract language and SLA for privacy controls.

3) Embeddings and derived data- Embeddings generated from customer text are treated as "Derived Data". For most customers we treat derived data as Customer Data for deletion/portability, subject to the DPA. We note that some features (e.g., shared model improvement programs) by default exclude persistent storage of embeddings unless explicitly enabled.

4) Subprocessors and flow-down- We will provide an initial subprocessors list (cloud provider, managed vector store, monitoring/metrics vendor). We notify customers of material additions and provide a 30-day objection window. We will flow down equivalent obligations to subprocessors.

Outstanding legal asks for contracting:
- Sophie: Please confirm whether a 30-day notification window for new subprocessors is acceptable and if you need the right to object (and what your approval/objection process is).
- Sophie: Any mandatory EU/EAA data transfer language you require (e.g., SCCs) for this account?

Action: attached summary includes proposed clause edits. If those look good, we can prepare DocuSign for signature. Laura — tagging you for two confirmations below about logs and subprocessors specifics for the SOW.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: DPA redlines and a few clarifying Qs

Rachel / Monica — quick engineering confirmation on the points you asked about. Short version below, happy to provide more detail or a SOW appendix with data flow diagrams.

1) Telemetry/logs- We collect: request metadata (timestamp, request size, model id, latency), error traces (stack/error ids), and infrastructure-level logs (node health). We do not persist raw customer inputs or outputs beyond the inference window unless the customer opts into logging for debugging. Retention: short-term request traces retained for 30 days, aggregated metrics for up to 2 years.

2) Embeddings- Embeddings generated via the embeddings endpoint are stored only if the customer calls the Redwood "persist/ index" API or enables "embedding retention" in their account settings. By default, embeddings are ephemeral. Where stored, embeddings are considered Customer Data and subject to deletion/portability requests.

3) Subprocessors (current list)
- Cloud infra: BigCloud Providers, Inc. (compute/VMs)
- Object storage: S3-compatible storage (Redwood-managed buckets)
- Vector store: VectorCo Managed DB (managed vector index service)
- Monitoring/metrics: Observant Metrics Ltd.
- Auth/KMS: KeySafe KMS (for envelope keys only)

We flow down DPA obligations to these subprocessors and maintain updated list at https://status.redwood.com/subprocessors (we can insert exact link in the contract). We aim to give a 30-day notice for new subprocessors, with an objection right for material changes.

If ProspectCorp wants SCCs or other EU transfer mechanisms, we can include either SCCs or an addendum that references standard contractual clauses.

Laura Bennett
Principal Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Barnes <sophie.barnes@prospectcorp.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Final proposed DPA language + DocuSign link

Hi Sophie — thanks for the patience while we pulled in legal and engineering. Attached is a redline summary that reflects the changes Rachel proposed and the technical confirmations from Laura. Highlights:

- Roles: Redwood confirmed as Processor; we accept language that makes the Controller/Processor mapping explicit (see attached redline).
- Telemetry: We propose the following contract text: "Redwood may collect operational telemetry (request metadata, error traces) for service operation and security. Redwood does not persist Customer Content beyond transient inference buffers unless Customer enables logging; operational logs retained up to 30 days, aggregated metrics up to 2 years."
- Embeddings: By default embeddings are ephemeral. Persisted embeddings (only stored if Customer enables persistence or uses Redwood-managed indexing) will be treated as Customer Data and are subject to deletion and portability.
- Subprocessors: Enclosed is our current subprocessors list and commitment to 30-day notice for new subprocessors. We will include SCCs or equivalent transfer mechanisms on EU accounts as required.

If these items look acceptable, we’ll issue a DocuSign envelope for the DPA. We’ve prepared a signing link here: https://app.docusign.com/some-sign-link/abcdef123456 and included the redline summary in Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c4d_redline_summary.

Please reply with any remaining objections by end of day Friday or we’ll proceed to final execution.

Best,
